reason: Anther-bearing means anthers are present on the part. Anther is PO_0009066 in the lexicon.
Gamosépale means the sepals are fused, which is connate.
Alveolar means honeycomb-pitted, which is alveolate.
Lagéniforme is French for flask-shaped.
Pseudo-axillary means only apparently axillary, not truly axillary. Extra-axillary means outside the axil, and the 'apparently' is lost. Keep the rule only if no better term exists.
Silloned is an English-text form of the French sillonné (furrowed), which is sulcate.
Cerebriform means brain-like with convoluted ridges. Rugose is the closest existing term and a new term is not worth it.
Glandular-tipped describes hairs with a gland at the tip. That is stipitate-glandular, not a glandular-pubescent indumentum.
Costulate means having small ribs, so ribbed fits.
Reticulate-nerved means the veins form a net, which is reticulate venation.
'Midvein extending' is ambiguous. It may extend beyond the apex (excurrent) or only to it. Percurrent means to the apex and not beyond, so this rule over-commits.
Checked bark is cracked into small blocks, which fits fissured (cracked).
Guttered means channelled or grooved.
Clustered is a synonym of aggregated, so the negation is fine.
Direct negation of rugose.
PO_0004544 has 'sucker' as a synonym, so not suckering means suckers are absent. Not suckering describes behaviour, which is a slightly looser reading.
PO_0025172 is thorn, so 'without thorns' means thorn absent.
Satiny means a soft sheen, and glistening (glossy, shiny) is the closest existing term.
Surculose means bearing suckers, and sucker is a synonym of PO_0004544.
Inodorous means without odour.
Channeled is a synonym of grooved, so the negation is fine.
Obcuneiform means inversely wedge-shaped, with the narrow end at the apex. Cuneate loses the 'ob-' and so reverses the orientation. Better as a new term, or reject.
Strangulate means abruptly constricted.
Vining is a climbing habit.
Gland-tipped hairs are glandular trichomes, so 'without' means they are absent.
Easily broken is brittle.
Hardly thickened means essentially not thickened.
Geniculate means sharply bent like a knee. 'Not geniculate' may still be curved or bent, so 'not bent' is too strong.
Direct negation of spreading.
Stalkless means sessile.
Tinged purple means faintly or partly purple. Purple loses the 'slightly' meaning.
Defined means distinct or clearly delimited, such as a defined margin. It does not mean conspicuous.
Semi-annular means half-ring, which is crescent-shaped.
Cirriform means tendril-like.
Pits holding glands are close to gland-dotted. No better existing term.
A long-tipped apex is acuminate (drawn out into a long point).
'Not clearly differentiated' means not distinct from a neighbouring part, for example calyx and corolla. It is not about conspicuousness.
Sheath-less means the sheath is missing, so the entity is absent. 'Not sheathing' means the part does not clasp, which is a different claim. Use sheath absent.
Stigmatose means having a stigma.
A trailer is a trailing, prostrate plant.
Tuft-like clusters are fascicled.
Defoliate means the leaves have been shed, which is a state or time-bound loss. It does not mean leaves are absent. Better as deciduous or leafless-at-time, or reject.
Radiculose means bearing rootlets or rhizoids, so the negation is rhizoid absent.
Compound corymb is a specific kind of inflorescence. Plain 'corymb present' loses 'compound'. Constrain it or leave unmapped.
A tendril-tipped rachis only exists on compound leaves. On a simple leaf the tendril is at the apex of the lamina.
Unisex is unisexual.
Variable-sized means size differs among individuals or samples. Unequal means parts differ within one structure. These are different characters.
Junciform means rush-like, which is slender and terete. Terete is the closest existing term.
Sillonné is French for furrowed or grooved.
Soudées is French for fused, which is connate.
